shloka_text: नर्मदापुलिने यत्र राक्षसेन्द्रः सुदारुणः । पुष्पोपहारं कुरुते तस्माद्देशाददूरतः ।। 7.32.1 ।।
transliteration: narmadāpuline yatra rākṣasendraḥ sudāruṇaḥ | puṣpopahāraṃ kurute tasmāddeśādadūrataḥ || 7.32.1 ||
translation: नर्मदापुलिने on the sandbank of the Narmada, यत्र where, राक्षसेन्द्रः the lord of Rakshasas, सुदारुणः very fierce, पुष्पोपहारम् an offering of flowers, कुरुते performs, तस्मात् from that, देशात् place, अदूरतः not far.
explanation: Not far from the place on the Narmada's sandbank where the very fierce lord of Rakshasas (Ravana) was performing his flower offering, another event was unfolding.
comments: Downstream, Kartavirya Arjuna dams the Narmada with his thousand arms, and the swollen flood sweeps away Ravana's offerings -- learning the cause, Ravana attacks; the armies clash, Prahasta is struck down, and Ravana and Arjuna duel with maces until Arjuna seizes the bewildered Ravana with his thousand arms and binds him as Vishnu bound Bali -- he bears Ravana captive into Mahishmati amid rejoicing.

shloka_text: अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो माहिष्मत्याः पतिः प्रभुः । क्रीडते सह नारीभिर्नर्मदातोयमाश्रितः ।। 7.32.2 ।।
transliteration: arjuno jayatāṃ śreṣṭho māhiṣmatyāḥ patiḥ prabhuḥ | krīḍate saha nārībhirnarmadātoyamāśritaḥ || 7.32.2 ||
translation: अर्जुनः Arjuna, जयताम् among the victorious, श्रेष्ठः the best, माहिष्मत्याः of Mahishmati, पतिः the lord, प्रभुः the powerful, क्रीडते plays, सह with, नारीभिः women, नर्मदातोयम् the waters of the Narmada, आश्रितः having resorted to.
explanation: Kartavirya Arjuna, the best among the victorious, the powerful lord of Mahishmati, was sporting with women near the waters of the Narmada.

shloka_text: तासां मध्यगतो राजा रराज च तदार्जुनः । करेणूनां सहस्रस्य मध्यस्थ इव कुञ्जरः ।। 7.32.3 ।।
transliteration: tāsāṃ madhyagato rājā rarāja ca tadārjunaḥ | kareṇūnāṃ sahasrasya madhyastha iva kuñjaraḥ || 7.32.3 ||
translation: तासां of them, मध्यगतो situated in the middle, राजा the king, रराज shone, च and, तदार्जुनः that Arjuna, करेणूनां of female elephants, सहस्रस्य of a thousand, मध्यस्थ situated in the middle, इव like, कुञ्जरः an elephant,
explanation: King Kartavirya Arjuna, situated amidst those women, shone splendidly, just like a male elephant standing in the midst of a thousand female elephants.

shloka_text: जिज्ञासुः स तु बाहूनां सहस्रस्योत्तमं बलम् । रुरोध नर्मदावेगं बाहुभिर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।। 7.32.4 ।।
transliteration: jijñāsuḥ sa tu bāhūnāṃ sahasrasyottamaṃ balam | rurodha narmadāvegaṃ bāhubhirbahubhirvṛtaḥ || 7.32.4 ||
translation: जिज्ञासुः desirous of knowing, सः he, तु indeed, बाहूनां of arms, सहस्रस्य of a thousand, उत्तमं supreme, बलम् strength, रुरोध he obstructed, नर्मदावेगं the current of the Narmada, बाहुभिः with arms, बहुभिः many, वृतः using,
explanation: Desirous of testing the supreme strength of his thousand arms, he indeed obstructed the flow of the Narmada river with his many arms.

shloka_text: कार्तवीर्यभुजासक्तं तज्जलं प्राप्य निर्मलम् । कूलोपहारं कुर्वाणं प्रतिस्रोतः प्रधावति ।। 7.32.5 ।।
transliteration: kārtavīryabhujāsaktaṃ tajjalaṃ prāpya nirmalam | kūlopahāraṃ kurvāṇaṃ pratisrotaḥ pradhāvati || 7.32.5 ||
translation: कार्तवीर्यभुजासक्तं held by Kartavirya's arms, तज्जलं that water, प्राप्य having reached, निर्मलम् pure, कूलोपहारं making an offering to the banks (overflowing), कुर्वाणं doing, प्रतिस्रोतः against the current, प्रधावति it rushes,
explanation: That pure water, held back by Kartavirya's arms, then rushed upstream, overflowing and making an offering to the river banks.

shloka_text: समीननक्रमकरः सपुष्पकुशसंस्तरः । स नर्मदाम्भसो वेगः प्रावृट्काल इवाबभौ ।। 7.32.6 ।।
transliteration: samīnanakramakaraḥ sapuṣpakuśasaṃstaraḥ | sa narmadāmbhaso vegaḥ prāvṛṭkāla ivābabhau || 7.32.6 ||
translation: समीननक्रमकरः with fish, crocodiles, and alligators, सपुष्पकुशसंस्तरः with flowers and kusha grass spread out, सः that, नर्मदाम्भसो of the Narmada's water, वेगः current, प्रावृट्काल the rainy season, इव like, अबबभौ it appeared,
explanation: That current of the Narmada's water, filled with fish, crocodiles, and alligators, and strewn with flowers and kusha grass, appeared like the rainy season itself.

shloka_text: स वेगः कार्तवीर्येण सम्प्रेषित इवाम्भसः । पुष्पोपहारं सकलं रावणस्य जहार ह ।। 7.32.7 ।।
transliteration: sa vegaḥ kārtavīryeṇa sampreṣita ivāmbhasaḥ | puṣpopahāraṃ sakalaṃ rāvaṇasya jahāra ha || 7.32.7 ||
translation: सः that, वेगः current, कार्तवीर्येण by Kartavirya, सम्प्रेषित sent forth, इव as if, अम्भसः of the water, पुष्पोपहारं flower offering, सकलं all, रावणस्य of Ravana, जहार carried away, ह indeed,
explanation: That current, as if propelled by Kartavirya's water, indeed carried away all of Ravana's flower offerings.

shloka_text: रावणो ऽर्धसमाप्तं तमुत्सृज्य नियमं तदा । नर्मदां पश्यते कान्तां प्रतिकूलां यथा प्रियाम् ।। 7.32.8 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇo 'rdhasamāptaṃ tamutsṛjya niyamaṃ tadā | narmadāṃ paśyate kāntāṃ pratikūlāṃ yathā priyām || 7.32.8 ||
translation: तदा then, रावणः Ravana, तं that, नियमं worship, अर्धसमाप्तम् half-finished, उत्सृज्य casting aside, कान्तां the lovely, नर्मदां Narmada, प्रतिकूलां flowing adversely, प्रियां यथा like a displeased beloved, पश्यते gazes upon.
explanation: Then Ravana, abandoning his half-finished worship, gazed upon the lovely Narmada flowing backward like a beloved turned away in displeasure.

shloka_text: पश्चिमेन तु तं दृष्ट्वा सागरोद्गारसन्निभम् । वर्धन्तमम्भसो वेगं पूर्वामाशां प्रविश्य तु ।। 7.32.9 ।।
transliteration: paścimena tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā sāgarodgārasannibham | vardhantamambhaso vegaṃ pūrvāmāśāṃ praviśya tu || 7.32.9 ||
translation: पश्चिमेन from the west, तु indeed, तम् that, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सागरोद्गारसन्निभम् resembling the gushing forth of the ocean, वर्धन्तम् increasing, अम्भसः of water, वेगम् the current, पूर्वाम् eastern, आशाम् direction, प्रविश्य having entered, तु indeed.
explanation: Having seen that increasing current of water, resembling the gushing forth of the ocean, entering the eastern direction from the west.

shloka_text: ततो ऽनुभ्रान्तशकुनां स्वभावोपरमे स्थिताम् । निर्विकाराङ्गनाभासामपश्यद्रावणो नदीम् ।। 7.32.10 ।।
transliteration: tato 'nubhrāntaśakunāṃ svabhāvoparame sthitām | nirvikārāṅganābhāsāmapaśyadrāvaṇo nadīm || 7.32.10 ||
translation: ततः then, अनुभ्रान्तशकुनाम् where birds were flying around, स्वभावोपरमे in the cessation of its natural state, स्थिताम् situated, निर्विकाराङ्गनाभासाम् appearing like an unperturbed woman, अपश्यत् saw, रावणः Ravana, नदीम् the river.
explanation: Then Ravana saw the river, where birds were flying around, situated in a state of cessation of its natural flow, appearing like an unperturbed woman.

shloka_text: सव्येतरकराङ्गुल्या सशब्दं च दशाननः । वेगप्रभावमन्वेष्टुं सो ऽदिशच्छुकसारणौ ।। 7.32.11 ।।
transliteration: savyetarakarāṅgulyā saśabdaṃ ca daśānanaḥ | vegaprabhāvamanveṣṭuṃ so 'diśacchukasāraṇau || 7.32.11 ||
translation: सव्येतरकराङ्गुल्या with the finger of his right hand, सशब्दम् loudly, च and, दशाननः Ravana, वेगप्रभावम् the effect of the current, अन्वेष्टुम् to investigate, सः he, अदिशत् ordered, शुकसारणौ Shuka and Sarana.
explanation: Ravana, with the finger of his right hand, loudly ordered Shuka and Sarana to investigate the effect of the current.

shloka_text: तौ तु रावणसन्दिष्टौ भ्रातरौ शुकसारणौ । व्योमान्तरगतौ वीरौ प्रस्थितौ पश्चिमामुखौ ।। 7.32.12 ।।
transliteration: tau tu rāvaṇasandiṣṭau bhrātarau śukasāraṇau | vyomāntaragatau vīrau prasthitau paścimāmukhau || 7.32.12 ||
translation: तौ those two, तु indeed, रावणसन्दिष्टौ ordered by Ravana, भ्रातरौ the two brothers, शुकसारणौ Shuka and Sarana, व्योमान्तरगतौ having gone into the sky, वीरौ the two heroes, प्रस्थितौ set out, पश्चिमामुखौ facing west.
explanation: Those two heroes, the brothers Shuka and Sarana, ordered by Ravana, set out facing west, having ascended into the sky.

shloka_text: अर्धयोजनमात्रं तु गत्वा तौ रजनीचरौ । पश्येतां पुरुषं तोये क्रीडन्तं सहयोषितम् ।। 7.32.13 ।।
transliteration: ardhayojanamātraṃ tu gatvā tau rajanīcarau | paśyetāṃ puruṣaṃ toye krīḍantaṃ sahayoṣitam || 7.32.13 ||
translation: अर्धयोजनमात्रम् only half a Yojana, तु indeed, गत्वा having gone, तौ those two, रजनीचरौ night-wanderers, पश्येताम् they saw, पुरुषम् a man, तोये in the water, क्रीडन्तम् playing, सहयोषितम् with a woman.
explanation: Having gone only half a Yojana, those two night-wanderers saw a man playing in the water with a woman.

shloka_text: बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशं तोयव्याकुलमूर्धजम् । मदरक्तान्तनयनं मदव्याकुलतेजसम् ।। 7.32.14 ।।
transliteration: bṛhatsālapratīkāśaṃ toyavyākulamūrdhajam | madaraktāntanayanaṃ madavyākulatejasam || 7.32.14 ||
translation: बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशम् resembling a great sala tree, तोयव्याकुलमूर्धजम् with hair dishevelled by water, मदरक्तान्तनयनम् with eyes red at the corners due to intoxication, मदव्याकुलतेजसम् with splendor agitated by intoxication.
explanation: He was like a great sala tree, his hair dishevelled by water, his eyes red at the corners from intoxication, and his might disturbed by the same.

shloka_text: नदीं बाहुसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमरिमर्दनम् । गिरिं पादसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमिव मेदिनीम् ।। 7.32.15 ।।
transliteration: nadīṃ bāhusahasreṇa rundhantamarimardanam | giriṃ pādasahasreṇa rundhantamiva medinīm || 7.32.15 ||
translation: नदीम् a river, बाहुसहस्रेण with a thousand arms, रुन्धन्तम् obstructing, अरिमर्दनम् the destroyer of enemies, गिरिम् a mountain, पादसहस्रेण with a thousand feet, रुन्धन्तम् obstructing, इव like, मेदिनीम् the earth.
explanation: He was obstructing the river with his thousand arms, like a mountain with a thousand feet obstructing the earth, a true destroyer of enemies.

shloka_text: बालानां वरनारीणां सहस्रेण समावृतम् । समदानां करेणूनां सहस्रेणेव कुञ्जरम् ।। 7.32.16 ।।
transliteration: bālānāṃ varanārīṇāṃ sahasreṇa samāvṛtam | samadānāṃ kareṇūnāṃ sahasreṇeva kuñjaram || 7.32.16 ||
translation: बालानाम् young, वरनारीणाम् excellent women, सहस्रेण with a thousand, समावृतम् surrounded, समदानाम् in rut, करेणूनाम् female elephants, सहस्रेण with a thousand, इव like, कुञ्जरम् a male elephant.
explanation: He was surrounded by a thousand young, excellent women, just as a male elephant is surrounded by a thousand female elephants in rut.

shloka_text: तमद्भुततमं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसौ शुकसारणौ । सन्निवृत्तावुपागम्य रावणं तमथोचतुः ।। 7.32.17 ।।
transliteration: tamadbhutatamaṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasau śukasāraṇau | sannivṛttāvupāgamya rāvaṇaṃ tamathocatuḥ || 7.32.17 ||
translation: तम् him, अद्भुततमम् most astonishing, दृष्ट्वा having seen, राक्षसौ the two rakshasas, शुकसारणौ Shuka and Sarana, सन्निवृत्तौ having returned, उपागम्य having approached, रावणम् Ravana, तम् him, अथ then, ऊचतुः spoke.
explanation: Having seen that most astonishing being, the two rakshasas, Shuka and Sarana, returned, approached Ravana, and then spoke to him.

shloka_text: बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशः को ऽप्यसौ राक्षसेश्वर । नर्मदां रोधवद्रुद्ध्वा क्रीडापयति योषितः ।। 7.32.18 ।।
transliteration: bṛhatsālapratīkāśaḥ ko 'pyasau rākṣaseśvara | narmadāṃ rodhavadruddhvā krīḍāpayati yoṣitaḥ || 7.32.18 ||
translation: बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशः resembling a great sala tree, कः who, अपि indeed, असौ this, राक्षसेश्वर O lord of rakshasas, नर्मदां the Narmada river, रोधवत् like a dam, रुद्ध्वा having obstructed, क्रीडापयति makes sport, योषितः with women.
explanation: They asked, "O lord of rakshasas, who is this being, resembling a great sala tree, who has obstructed the Narmada river like a dam and is sporting with women?"

shloka_text: तेन बाहुसहस्रेण सन्निरुद्धजला नदी । सागरोद्गारसङ्काशानुद्गारान्सृजते मुहुः ।। 7.32.19 ।।
transliteration: tena bāhusahasreṇa sanniruddhajalā nadī | sāgarodgārasaṅkāśānudgārānsṛjate muhuḥ || 7.32.19 ||
translation: तेन by that, बाहुसहस्रेण by thousand arms, सन्निरुद्धजला having its water obstructed, नदी the river, सागरोद्गारसङ्काशान् resembling the eruptions of the ocean, उद्गारान् eruptions, सृजते emits, मुहुः repeatedly.
explanation: Due to his thousand arms obstructing its waters, the river repeatedly emitted eruptions of water resembling the ocean's surges.

shloka_text: इत्येवं भाषमाणौ तौ निशाम्य शुकसारणौ । रावणो ऽर्जुन इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ युद्धलालसः ।। 7.32.20 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ bhāṣamāṇau tau niśāmya śukasāraṇau | rāvaṇo 'rjuna ityuktvā prayayau yuddhalālasaḥ || 7.32.20 ||
translation: इति thus, एवम् in this manner, भाषमाणौ speaking, तौ those two, निशाम्य having heard, शुकसारणौ Shuka and Sarana, रावणः Ravana, अर्जुन Arjuna, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, प्रययौ went forth, युद्धलालसः eager for battle.
explanation: Having heard Shuka and Sarana speaking thus, Ravana, eager for battle, declared "Arjuna!" and set forth.

shloka_text: अर्जुनाभिमुखे तस्मिन्रावणे राक्षसाधिपे । चण्डः प्रवाति पवनः सनादः सुरजास्तथा ।। 7.32.21 ।।
transliteration: arjunābhimukhe tasminrāvaṇe rākṣasādhipe | caṇḍaḥ pravāti pavanaḥ sanādaḥ surajāstathā || 7.32.21 ||
translation: अर्जुनाभिमुखे facing Arjuna, तस्मिन् in that, रावणे Ravana, राक्षसाधिपे the lord of Rakshasas, चण्डः fierce, प्रवाति blows, पवनः wind, सनादः with sound, सुरजाः divine dust, तथा and so.
explanation: As Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, faced Arjuna, a fierce, roaring wind blew, and divine dust arose, indicating ill omens.

shloka_text: सकृदेव कृतो रावः सरक्तः प्रेषितो घनैः । महोदरमहापार्श्वधूम्राक्षशुकसारणैः ।। 7.32.22 ।।
transliteration: sakṛdeva kṛto rāvaḥ saraktaḥ preṣito ghanaiḥ | mahodaramahāpārśvadhūmrākṣaśukasāraṇaiḥ || 7.32.22 ||
translation: सकृदेव just once, कृतः made, रावः a cry, सरक्तः bloody, प्रेषितः sent forth, घनैः by clouds, महोदरमहापार्श्वधूम्राक्षशुकसारणैः by Mahodara, Mahaparshva, Dhumraksha, Shuka, and Sarana.
explanation: A single bloody cry was emitted by the clouds as an omen, while Ravana was accompanied by Mahodara, Mahaparshva, Dhumraksha, Shuka, and Sarana.

shloka_text: संवृतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तत्रागाद्यत्र चार्जुनः । अदीर्घेणैव कालेन स तदा राक्षसो बली । तं नर्मदाह्रदं भीममाजगामाञ्जनप्रभः ।। 7.32.23 ।।
transliteration: saṃvṛto rākṣasendrastu tatrāgādyatra cārjunaḥ | adīrgheṇaiva kālena sa tadā rākṣaso balī | taṃ narmadāhradaṃ bhīmamājagāmāñjanaprabhaḥ || 7.32.23 ||
translation: संवृतः surrounded, राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु but the lord of Rakshasas, तत्र there, अगात् went, यत्र where, च and, अर्जुनः Arjuna, अदीर्घेण not long, एव indeed, कालेन by time, सः he, तदा then, राक्षसः Rakshasa, बली powerful, तम् that, नर्मदाह्रदम् Narmada pool, भीमम् terrible, आजगाम came, अञ्जनप्रभः shining like collyrium.
explanation: The lord of Rakshasas, surrounded by his retinue, quickly arrived at the terrible Narmada pool where Arjuna was, that powerful Rakshasa himself shining like collyrium.

shloka_text: स तत्र स्त्रीपरिवृतं वाशिताभिरिव द्विपम् । नरेन्द्रं पश्यते राजा राक्षसानां तदार्जुनम् ।। 7.32.24 ।।
transliteration: sa tatra strīparivṛtaṃ vāśitābhiriva dvipam | narendraṃ paśyate rājā rākṣasānāṃ tadārjunam || 7.32.24 ||
translation: सः He, तत्र there, स्त्रीपरिवृतं surrounded by women, वाशिताभिः by female elephants, इव like, द्विपम् an elephant, नरेन्द्रं the king (of men), पश्यते sees, राजा the king, राक्षसानां of the Rākṣasas, तत् that, अर्जुनम् Arjuna (Kartavirya Arjuna)
explanation: The king of Rākṣasas, Ravana, there saw that King Arjuna, the king of men, surrounded by women, just like an elephant surrounded by female elephants.

shloka_text: स रोषाद्रक्तनयनो राक्षसेन्द्रो बलोद्धतः ।। 7.32.25 ।।
transliteration: sa roṣādraktanayano rākṣasendro baloddhataḥ || 7.32.25 ||
translation: सः He, रोषात् from anger, रक्तनयनः with red eyes, राक्षसेन्द्रः the king of Rākṣasas, बलोद्धतः arrogant with strength
explanation: He, the king of Rākṣasas, arrogant with his power, had his eyes red with anger.

shloka_text: इत्येवमर्जुनामात्यनाह गम्भीरया गिरा । अमात्याः क्षिप्रमाख्यात हैहयस्य नृपस्य वै ।। 7.32.26 ।।
transliteration: ityevamarjunāmātyanāha gambhīrayā girā | amātyāḥ kṣipramākhyāta haihayasya nṛpasya vai || 7.32.26 ||
translation: इति thus, एवम् in this manner, अर्जुन-अमात्यान् to Arjuna's ministers, आह said, गम्भीरया with a deep, गिरा voice, अमात्याः O ministers, क्षिप्रम् quickly, आख्यात inform, हैहयस्य of the Haihaya, नृपस्य of the king, वै indeed
explanation: He thus spoke to Arjuna's ministers in a deep voice, saying, "O ministers, quickly inform the Haihaya king."

shloka_text: युद्धार्थी समनुप्राप्तो रावणो नाम राक्षसः । रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणो ऽथार्जुनस्य ते । उत्तस्थुः सायुधास्त्राश्च रावणं वाक्यमब्रुवन् ।। 7.32.27 ।।
transliteration: yuddhārthī samanuprāpto rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ | rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā mantriṇo 'thārjunasya te | uttasthuḥ sāyudhāstrāśca rāvaṇaṃ vākyamabruvan || 7.32.27 ||
translation: युद्धार्थी desirous of battle, समनुप्राप्तः has arrived, रावणः Ravana, नाम named, राक्षसः a Rākṣasa, रावणस्य Ravana's, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, मन्त्रिणः the ministers, अथ then, अर्जुनस्य of Arjuna, ते those, उत्तस्थुः stood up, सायुधास्त्राः with weapons and missiles, च and, रावणम् to Ravana, वाक्यम् words, अब्रुवन् spoke
explanation: Having heard Ravana's words, "A Rākṣasa named Ravana, desirous of battle, has arrived," those ministers of Arjuna then stood up with their weapons and missiles and spoke to Ravana.

shloka_text: युद्धस्य कालो विज्ञेयः साधु भोः साधु रावण ।। 7.32.28 ।।
transliteration: yuddhasya kālo vijñeyaḥ sādhu bhoḥ sādhu rāvaṇa || 7.32.28 ||
translation: युद्धस्य of battle, कालः the time, विज्ञेयः should be known, साधु well done, भोः O, साधु well done, रावण O Ravana
explanation: The ministers said, "The time for battle should be known; well done, O Ravana, well done!"

shloka_text: चः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणो ऽथार्जुनस्य ते । यः क्षीबं स्त्रीवृतं चैव योद्धुमुत्सहते नृपम् । स्त्रीसमक्षं कथं यत्तद्योद्धुमुत्सहसे ऽर्जुनम् । वाशितामध्यगं मत्तं शार्दूल इव कुञ्जरम् ।। 7.32.29 ।।
transliteration: caḥ śrutvā mantriṇo 'thārjunasya te | yaḥ kṣībaṃ strīvṛtaṃ caiva yoddhumutsahate nṛpam | strīsamakṣaṃ kathaṃ yattadyoddhumutsahase 'rjunam | vāśitāmadhyagaṃ mattaṃ śārdūla iva kuñjaram || 7.32.29 ||
translation: चः and, श्रुत्वा having heard, मन्त्रिणो of the ministers, अथार्जुनस्य then of Arjuna, ते they, यः who, क्षीबं intoxicated, स्त्रीवृतं surrounded by women, चैव and indeed, योद्धुमुत्सहते desires to fight, नृपम् the king, स्त्रीसमक्षं in the presence of women, कथं how, यत्तत् that which, योद्धुमुत्सहसे you desire to fight, अर्जुनम् Arjuna, वाशितामध्यगं being amidst female elephants, मत्तं intoxicated, शार्दूल a tiger, इव like, कुञ्जरम् an elephant.
explanation: Ravana's ministers, having heard Arjuna's ministers, questioned Ravana why he desired to fight an intoxicated king surrounded by women, comparing it to a tiger attacking an intoxicated elephant amidst female elephants.

shloka_text: क्षमस्वाद्य दशग्रीव चोष्यतां रजनी त्वया । युद्धे श्रद्धा च यद्यस्ति श्वस्तात समरे ऽर्जुनम् ।। 7.32.30 ।।
transliteration: kṣamasvādya daśagrīva coṣyatāṃ rajanī tvayā | yuddhe śraddhā ca yadyasti śvastāta samare 'rjunam || 7.32.30 ||
translation: क्षमस्वाद्य forgive today, दशग्रीव O ten-necked one, चोष्यतां let it be spent, रजनी the night, त्वया by you, युद्धे in battle, श्रद्धा desire, च and, यद्यस्ति if there is, श्वस्तात tomorrow, O dear one, समरे in battle, अर्जुनम् Arjuna.
explanation: Ravana's ministers advised him to forgive Arjuna for today and spend the night, suggesting that if he still desired battle, he could fight Arjuna tomorrow.

shloka_text: यद्यद्यास्ति मतिर्योद्धुं युद्धतृष्णासमावृता । निहत्यास्मांस्ततो युद्धमर्जुनेनोपयास्यसि ।। 7.32.31 ।।
transliteration: yadyadyāsti matiryoddhuṃ yuddhatṛṣṇāsamāvṛtā | nihatyāsmāṃstato yuddhamarjunenopayāsyasi || 7.32.31 ||
translation: यद्यद्यास्ति if even today there is, मतिर्योद्धुं a mind to fight, युद्धतृष्णासमावृता enveloped by battle-thirst, निहत्यास्मांस्ततो having killed us then, युद्धमर्जुनेनोपयास्यसि you will engage in battle with Arjuna.
explanation: The ministers further challenged Ravana, stating that if he was still consumed by the thirst for battle today, he would first have to defeat them before he could fight Arjuna.

shloka_text: ततस्ते रावणामात्यैरमात्याः पार्थिवस्य तु । सूदिताश्चापि ते युद्धे भक्षिताश्च बुभुक्षितैः ।। 7.32.32 ।।
transliteration: tataste rāvaṇāmātyairamātyāḥ pārthivasya tu | sūditāścāpi te yuddhe bhakṣitāśca bubhukṣitaiḥ || 7.32.32 ||
translation: ततस्ते then they, रावणामात्यैः by Ravana's ministers, अमात्याः the ministers, पार्थिवस्य of the king, तु indeed, सूदिताश्चापि were killed and also, ते they, युद्धे in battle, भक्षिताश्च and devoured, बुभुक्षितैः by the hungry ones.
explanation: Subsequently, Arjuna's ministers were killed and even devoured in battle by Ravana's hungry ministers.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दो नर्मदातीर आबभौ । अर्जुनस्यानुयातऽणां रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणाम् ।। 7.32.33 ।।
transliteration: tato halahalāśabdo narmadātīra ābabhau | arjunasyānuyāta'ṇāṃ rāvaṇasya ca mantriṇām || 7.32.33 ||
translation: ततो then, हलहलाशब्दो a tumultuous sound, नर्मदातीर on the bank of Narmada, आबभौ arose, अर्जुनस्यानुयातऽणां of Arjuna's followers, रावणस्य of Ravana, च and, मन्त्रिणाम् of the ministers.
explanation: Then, a great tumultuous sound arose on the bank of the Narmada, emanating from the followers of Arjuna and the ministers of Ravana.

shloka_text: इषुभिस्तोमरैः शूलैस्त्रिशूलैर्वज्रकर्षणैः । सरावणानर्दयन्तः समन्तात्समभिद्रुताः ।। 7.32.34 ।।
transliteration: iṣubhistomaraiḥ śūlaistriśūlairvajrakarṣaṇaiḥ | sarāvaṇānardayantaḥ samantātsamabhidrutāḥ || 7.32.34 ||
translation: इषुभिः with arrows, तोमरैः with lances, शूलैः with spears, त्रिशूलैः with tridents, वज्रकर्षणैः with thunderbolt-like weapons, सरावणान् along with Ravana, अर्दयन्तः tormenting, समन्तात् from all sides, समभिद्रुताः attacked.
explanation: They attacked from all sides, tormenting Ravana and his forces with arrows, lances, spears, tridents, and thunderbolt-like weapons.

shloka_text: हैहयाधिपयोधानां वेग आसीत्सुदारुणः । सनक्रमीनमकरसमुद्रस्येव निःस्वनः ।। 7.32.35 ।।
transliteration: haihayādhipayodhānāṃ vega āsītsudāruṇaḥ | sanakramīnamakarasamudrasyeva niḥsvanaḥ || 7.32.35 ||
translation: हैहयाधिपयोधानाम् of the warriors of the Haihaya king, वेगः the force, आसीत् was, सुदारुणः very terrible, सनक्रमीनमकरसमुद्रस्य of a sea with crocodiles, fish, and alligators, इव like, निःस्वनः the roar.
explanation: The force of the Haihaya king's warriors was exceedingly terrible, like the roar of an ocean filled with crocodiles, fish, and alligators.

shloka_text: रावणस्य तु ते ऽमात्याः प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः । कार्तवीर्यबलं क्रुद्धा निर्दहन्ति स्म तेजसा ।। 7.32.36 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇasya tu te 'mātyāḥ prahastaśukasāraṇāḥ | kārtavīryabalaṃ kruddhā nirdahanti sma tejasā || 7.32.36 ||
translation: रावणस्य Ravana's, तु indeed, ते those, अमात्याः ministers, प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः Prahasta, Shuka, Sarana, कार्तवीर्यबलम् Kartavirya's army, क्रुद्धाः enraged, निर्दहन्ति स्म were burning, तेजसा with their might.
explanation: Ravana's ministers, Prahasta, Shuka, and Sarana, enraged, were indeed destroying Kartavirya's army with their fierce might.

shloka_text: अर्जुनाय तु तत्कर्म रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः । क्रीडमानाय कथितं पुरुषैर्द्वाररक्षिभिः ।। 7.32.37 ।।
transliteration: arjunāya tu tatkarma rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ | krīḍamānāya kathitaṃ puruṣairdvārarakṣibhiḥ || 7.32.37 ||
translation: अर्जुनाय to Arjuna, तु indeed, तत्कर्म that deed, रावणस्य of Ravana, समन्त्रिणः with his ministers, क्रीडमानाय who was playing, कथितम् was told, पुरुषैः by men, द्वाररक्षिभिः by gatekeepers.
explanation: That deed of Ravana and his ministers was indeed reported to Arjuna, who was then engaged in sport, by the gatekeepers.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा न भेतव्यमिति स्त्रीजनं तं ततो ऽर्जुनः । उत्ततार जलात्तस्माद्गङ्गातोयादिवाञ्जनः ।। 7.32.38 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā na bhetavyamiti strījanaṃ taṃ tato 'rjunaḥ | uttatāra jalāttasmādgaṅgātoyādivāñjanaḥ || 7.32.38 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, न not, भेतव्यम् to be feared, इति thus, स्त्रीजनम् to the womenfolk, तम् them, ततः then, अर्जुनः Arjuna, उत्ततार rose up, जलात् from the water, तस्मात् from that, गङ्गातोयात् from the waters of Ganga, इव like, अञ्जनः Anjana (mountain).
explanation: Having heard the news, Arjuna then reassured the womenfolk not to fear, and emerged from the water like the Anjana mountain rising from the waters of the Ganga.

shloka_text: क्रोधदूषितनेत्रस्तु स ततो ऽर्जुनपावकः । प्रजज्वाल महाघोरो युगान्त इव पावकः ।। 7.32.39 ।।
transliteration: krodhadūṣitanetrastu sa tato 'rjunapāvakaḥ | prajajvāla mahāghoro yugānta iva pāvakaḥ || 7.32.39 ||
translation: क्रोधदूषितनेत्रस्तु whose eyes were reddened by anger, सः he, ततः then, अर्जुनपावकः Arjuna who was like fire, प्रजज्वाल blazed forth, महाघोरः exceedingly terrible, युगान्ते at the end of an eon, इव like, पावकः fire.
explanation: Then, Arjuna, whose eyes were red with anger and who was like a blazing fire, shone forth with terrible intensity, like the destructive fire at the end of an eon.

shloka_text: स तूर्णतरमादाय वरहेमाङ्गदो गदाम् । अभिदुद्राव रक्षांसि तमांसीव दिवाकरः ।। 7.32.40 ।।
transliteration: sa tūrṇataramādāya varahemāṅgado gadām | abhidudrāva rakṣāṃsi tamāṃsīva divākaraḥ || 7.32.40 ||
translation: सः he, तूर्णतरम् very quickly, आदाय taking, वरहेमाङ्गदः adorned with excellent golden armlets, गदाम् mace, अभिदुद्राव rushed towards, रक्षांसि the Rākṣasas, तमांसी darkness, इव like, दिवाकरः the sun.
explanation: Adorned with splendid golden armlets, he swiftly seized his mace and charged at the Rākṣasas, just as the sun dispels darkness.

shloka_text: बाहुविक्षेपकरणां समुद्यम्य महागदाम् । गारुडं वेगमास्थाय चापपातैव सो ऽर्जुनः ।। 7.32.41 ।।
transliteration: bāhuvikṣepakaraṇāṃ samudyamya mahāgadām | gāruḍaṃ vegamāsthāya cāpapātaiva so 'rjunaḥ || 7.32.41 ||
translation: बाहुविक्षेपकरणाम् causing the arms to swing, समुद्यम्य lifting up, महागदाम् the great mace, गारुडम् of Garuda, वेगम् speed, आस्थाय assuming, च and, अपपात fell upon, एव indeed, सः he, अर्जुनः Arjuna.
explanation: Lifting his mighty mace, which caused his arms to swing, Arjuna rushed forward with the speed of Garuda.

shloka_text: तस्य मार्गं समारुद्ध्य विन्ध्यो ऽर्कस्येव पर्वतः । स्थितो विन्ध्य इवाकम्प्यः प्रहस्तो मुसलायुधः ।। 7.32.42 ।।
transliteration: tasya mārgaṃ samāruddhya vindhyo 'rkasyeva parvataḥ | sthito vindhya ivākampyaḥ prahasto musalāyudhaḥ || 7.32.42 ||
translation: तस्य his, मार्गम् path, समारुद्ध्य obstructing, विन्ध्यः Vindhya, अर्कस्य of the sun, इव like, पर्वतः mountain, स्थितः stood, विन्ध्यः Vindhya, इव like, अकम्प्यः unshakable, प्रहस्तः Prahasta, मुसलायुधः armed with a mace.
explanation: Prahasta, armed with a mace, stood in Arjuna's path, obstructing him like the Vindhya mountain blocking the sun, and was as unshakable as the Vindhya itself.

shloka_text: ततो ऽस्य मुसलं घोरं लोहबद्धं महोद्धतः । प्रहस्तः प्रेषयन्क्रुद्धो ररास च यथाम्बुदः ।। 7.32.43 ।।
transliteration: tato 'sya musalaṃ ghoraṃ lohabaddhaṃ mahoddhataḥ | prahastaḥ preṣayankruddho rarāsa ca yathāmbudaḥ || 7.32.43 ||
translation: ततः then, अस्य at him, मुसलम् mace, घोरम् terrible, लोहबद्धम् bound with iron, महोद्धतः very arrogant, प्रहस्तः Prahasta, प्रेषयन् hurling, क्रुद्धः enraged, ररास roared, च and, यथा like, अम्बुदः a cloud.
explanation: Then, the enraged and arrogant Prahasta hurled his terrible, iron-bound mace at Arjuna and roared like a thunderous cloud.

shloka_text: तस्याग्रे मुसलस्याग्निरशोकापीडसन्निभः । प्रहस्तकरमुक्तस्य बभूव प्रदहन्निव ।। 7.32.44 ।।
transliteration: tasyāgre musalasyāgniraśokāpīḍasannibhaḥ | prahastakaramuktasya babhūva pradahanniva || 7.32.44 ||
translation: तस्य its, अग्रे in front, मुसलस्य of the mace, अग्निः fire, अशोकापीडसन्निभः resembling a garland of Ashoka flowers, प्रहस्तकरमुक्तस्य released by Prahasta's hand, बभूव became, प्रदहन् burning, इव as if.
explanation: In front of the mace released by Prahasta's hand, a fire, resembling a garland of Ashoka flowers, appeared as if burning.

shloka_text: अथायान्तं तु मुसलं कार्तवीर्यस्तदार्जुनः । निपुणं वञ्चयामास सगदो ऽगदविक्रमः ।। 7.32.45 ।।
transliteration: athāyāntaṃ tu musalaṃ kārtavīryastadārjunaḥ | nipuṇaṃ vañcayāmāsa sagado 'gadavikramaḥ || 7.32.45 ||
translation: अथ then, आयान्तं coming, तु indeed, मुसलं mace, कार्तवीर्यः Kartavirya, तत् that, अर्जुनः Arjuna, निपुणं skillfully, वञ्चयामास dodged, सगदः with his mace, अगदविक्रमः of unimpaired valor.
explanation: Then, Kartavirya Arjuna, of unimpaired valor and holding his mace, skillfully dodged that incoming mace.

shloka_text: ततस्तमभिदुद्राव प्रहस्तं हैहयाधिपः । भ्रामयानो गदां गुर्वीं पञ्चबाहुशतोच्छ्रयाम् ।। 7.32.46 ।।
transliteration: tatastamabhidudrāva prahastaṃ haihayādhipaḥ | bhrāmayāno gadāṃ gurvīṃ pañcabāhuśatocchrayām || 7.32.46 ||
translation: ततः thereafter, तं him, अभिदुद्राव rushed towards, प्रहस्तं Prahasta, हैहयाधिपः the lord of Haihayas, भ्रामयानः whirling, गदां mace, गुर्वीं heavy, पञ्चबाहुशतोच्छ्रयाम् as high as five hundred arms.
explanation: Thereafter, the lord of Haihayas rushed towards Prahasta, whirling his heavy mace, which was as high as five hundred arms.

shloka_text: तथा हतो ऽतिवेगेन प्रहस्तो गदया तदा । निपपात स्थितः शैलो वज्रिवज्रहतो यथा ।। 7.32.47 ।।
transliteration: tathā hato 'tivegena prahasto gadayā tadā | nipapāta sthitaḥ śailo vajrivajrahato yathā || 7.32.47 ||
translation: तथा thus, हतः struck, अतिवेगेन with great force, प्रहस्तः Prahasta, गदया by the mace, तदा then, निपपात fell down, स्थितः standing, शैलः mountain, वज्रिवज्रहतः struck by Indra's thunderbolt, यथा as.
explanation: Thus struck by the mace with great force, Prahasta then fell down, like a standing mountain struck by Indra's thunderbolt.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तं पतितं दृष्ट्वा मारीचशुकसारणाः । समहोदरधूम्राक्षा ह्यपसृष्टा रणाजिरात् ।। 7.32.48 ।।
transliteration: prahastaṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mārīcaśukasāraṇāḥ | samahodaradhūmrākṣā hyapasṛṣṭā raṇājirāt || 7.32.48 ||
translation: प्रहस्तं Prahasta, पतितं fallen, दृष्ट्वा having seen, मारीचशुकसारणाः Maricha, Shuka, and Sarana, समहोदरधूम्राक्षाः with Mahodara and Dhumraksha, हि indeed, अपसृष्टाः fled, रणाजिरात् from the battlefield.
explanation: Having seen Prahasta fallen, Maricha, Shuka, Sarana, along with Mahodara and Dhumraksha, indeed fled from the battlefield.

shloka_text: अपक्रान्तेष्वमात्येषु प्रहस्ते वै निपातिते । रावणो ऽभ्यद्रवत्तूर्णमर्जुनं नृपसत्तमम् ।। 7.32.49 ।।
transliteration: apakrānteṣvamātyeṣu prahaste vai nipātite | rāvaṇo 'bhyadravattūrṇamarjunaṃ nṛpasattamam || 7.32.49 ||
translation: अपक्रान्तेषु when departed, अमात्येषु the ministers, प्रहस्ते Prahasta, वै indeed, निपातिते having been struck down, रावणः Ravana, अभ्यद्रवत् rushed towards, तूर्णम् quickly, अर्जुनम् Arjuna, नृपसत्तमम् the best among kings,
explanation: After his ministers had retreated and Prahasta was killed, Ravana quickly rushed towards Kartavirya Arjuna, the best among kings.

shloka_text: सहस्रबाहोस्तद्युद्धं विंशद्बाहोश्च दारुणम् । नृपराक्षसयोस्तत्र चारब्धं रोमहर्षणम् ।। 7.32.50 ।।
transliteration: sahasrabāhostadyuddhaṃ viṃśadbāhośca dāruṇam | nṛparākṣasayostatra cārabdhaṃ romaharṣaṇam || 7.32.50 ||
translation: सहस्रबाहोः of the one with a thousand arms, तत् that, युद्धम् battle, विंशद्बाहोः of the one with twenty arms, च and, दारुणम् terrible, नृपराक्षसयोः of the king and the demon, तत्र there, च and, आरब्धम् began, रोमहर्षणम् hair-raising,
explanation: There, a terrible and hair-raising battle began between the king with a thousand arms (Arjuna) and the demon with twenty arms (Ravana).

shloka_text: सागराविव संरब्धौ चलन्मूलाविवाचलौ । तेजोयुक्ताविवादित्यौ प्रदहन्ताविवानलौ ।। 7.32.51 ।।
transliteration: sāgarāviva saṃrabdhau calanmūlāvivācalau | tejoyuktāvivādityau pradahantāvivānalau || 7.32.51 ||
translation: सागराविव like two oceans, संरब्धौ enraged, चलन्मूलौ with moving roots, इव like, अचलौ two mountains, तेजोयुक्तौ endowed with splendor, इव like, आदित्यौ two suns, प्रदहन्तौ burning, इव like, अनलौ two fires,
explanation: They were enraged like two oceans, like two mountains with their roots shaking, like two suns full of splendor, and like two burning fires.

shloka_text: बलोद्धतौ यथा नागौ वाशितार्थे यथा वृषौ । मेघाविव विनर्दन्तौ सिंहाविव बलोत्कटौ ।। 7.32.52 ।।
transliteration: baloddhatau yathā nāgau vāśitārthe yathā vṛṣau | meghāviva vinardantau siṃhāviva balotkaṭau || 7.32.52 ||
translation: बलोद्धतौ arrogant with strength, यथा like, नागौ two elephants, वाशितार्थे for the sake of a female, यथा like, वृषौ two bulls, मेघाविव like two clouds, विनर्दन्तौ roaring, सिंहाविव like two lions, बलोत्कटौ exceedingly strong,
explanation: They were like two elephants arrogant with strength, like two bulls fighting over a cow, like two roaring clouds, and like two exceedingly strong lions.

shloka_text: रुद्रकालाविव क्रुद्धौ तदा तौ राक्षसार्जुनौ । परस्परं गदाभ्यां तौ ताडयामासतुर्भृशम् ।। 7.32.53 ।।
transliteration: rudrakālāviva kruddhau tadā tau rākṣasārjunau | parasparaṃ gadābhyāṃ tau tāḍayāmāsaturbhṛśam || 7.32.53 ||
translation: रुद्रकालौ Rudra and Kala, इव like, क्रुद्धौ enraged, तदा then, तौ those two, राक्षसार्जुनौ the demon and Arjuna, परस्परम् each other, गदाभ्याम् with maces, तौ those two, ताडयामासतुः struck, भृशम् fiercely,
explanation: Then, those two, the demon Ravana and Arjuna, enraged like Rudra and Kala, fiercely struck each other with their maces.

shloka_text: वज्रप्रहारानचला यथा घोरान्विषेहिरे । गदाप्रहारांस्तौ तत्र सेहाते नरराक्षसौ ।। 7.32.54 ।।
transliteration: vajraprahārānacalā yathā ghorānviṣehire | gadāprahārāṃstau tatra sehāte nararākṣasau || 7.32.54 ||
translation: वज्रप्रहारान् thunderbolt strikes, अचलाः mountains, यथा just as, घोरान् terrible, विषेहिरे endured, गदाप्रहारान् mace strikes, तौ those two, तत्र there, सेहाते endured, नरराक्षसौ the man and the demon.
explanation: Just as mountains endure terrible thunderbolt strikes, so too did the man (Arjuna) and the demon (Ravana) endure each other's mace strikes in that battle.

shloka_text: यथा ऽ शनिरवेभ्यस्तु जायते ऽथ प्रतिश्रुतिः । तथा तयोर्गदापोथैर्दिशः सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुताः ।। 7.32.55 ।।
transliteration: yathā ' śaniravebhyastu jāyate 'tha pratiśrutiḥ | tathā tayorgadāpothairdiśaḥ sarvāḥ pratiśrutāḥ || 7.32.55 ||
translation: यथा just as, अशनिरवेभ्यः from the sounds of thunder, तु indeed, जायते arises, अथ then, प्रतिश्रुतिः echo, तथा similarly, तयोः of those two, गदापोथैः by the impacts of maces, दिशः directions, सर्वाः all, प्रतिश्रुताः echoed.
explanation: Just as an echo arises from the sounds of thunder, similarly, all directions reverberated with the impacts of their maces.

shloka_text: अर्जुनस्य गदा सा तु पात्यमाना ऽहितोरसि । काञ्चनाभं नभश्चक्रे विद्युत्सौदामिनी यथा ।। 7.32.56 ।।
transliteration: arjunasya gadā sā tu pātyamānā 'hitorasi | kāñcanābhaṃ nabhaścakre vidyutsaudāminī yathā || 7.32.56 ||
translation: अर्जुनस्य of Arjuna, गदा mace, सा that, तु indeed, पात्यमाना being struck, अहितोरसि on the chest of the enemy, काञ्चनाभम् golden-hued, नभः sky, चक्रे made, विद्युत् lightning, सौदामिनी a flash of lightning, यथा just as.
explanation: Arjuna's mace, when struck upon the enemy's (Ravana's) chest, made the sky appear golden-hued, just like a flash of lightning.

shloka_text: तथैव रावणेनापि पात्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः । अर्जुनोरसि निर्भाति गदोल्केव महागिरौ ।। 7.32.57 ।।
transliteration: tathaiva rāvaṇenāpi pātyamānā muhurmuhuḥ | arjunorasi nirbhāti gadolkeva mahāgirau || 7.32.57 ||
translation: तथैव similarly, रावणेन by Ravana, अपि also, पात्यमाना being struck, मुहुर्मुहुः again and again, अर्जुनोरसि on Arjuna's chest, निर्भाति shone, गदोल्का a mace-meteor, इव like, महागिरौ on a great mountain.
explanation: Similarly, Ravana's mace, struck repeatedly on Arjuna's chest, shone like a meteor striking a great mountain.

shloka_text: नार्जुनः खेदमायाति न राक्षसगणेश्वरः । इदमासीत्तयोर्युद्धं यथा पूर्वं बलीन्द्रयोः ।। 7.32.58 ।।
transliteration: nārjunaḥ khedamāyāti na rākṣasagaṇeśvaraḥ | idamāsīttayoryuddhaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ balīndrayoḥ || 7.32.58 ||
translation: न not, अर्जुनः Arjuna, खेदम् weariness, आयाति attained, न nor, राक्षसगणेश्वरः the lord of the demon hosts, इदम् this, आसीत् was, तयोः of those two, युद्धम् battle, यथा like, पूर्वम् formerly, बलीन्द्रयोः of Bali and Indra.
explanation: Neither Arjuna nor the lord of the demon hosts (Ravana) showed any weariness, and their battle was like the ancient conflict between Bali and Indra.

shloka_text: शृङ्गैरिव वृषायुध्यन्दन्ताग्रैरिव कुञ्जरौ । परस्परं तौ निघ्नन्तौ नरराक्षससत्तमौ ।। 7.32.59 ।।
transliteration: śṛṅgairiva vṛṣāyudhyandantāgrairiva kuñjarau | parasparaṃ tau nighnantau nararākṣasasattamau || 7.32.59 ||
translation: शृङ्गैरिव like with horns, वृषायुध्यन् two bulls fighting, दन्ताग्रैरिव like with the tips of tusks, कुञ्जरौ two elephants, परस्परं each other, तौ those two, निघ्नन्तौ striking, नरराक्षससत्तमौ the best of humans and demons.
explanation: The two, the best among humans and demons, struck each other like two bulls fighting with their horns or two elephants with the tips of their tusks.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्जुनेन क्रुद्धेन सर्वप्राणेन सा गदा । स्तनयोरन्तरे मुक्ता रावणस्य महोरसि ।। 7.32.60 ।।
transliteration: tato 'rjunena kruddhena sarvaprāṇena sā gadā | stanayorantare muktā rāvaṇasya mahorasi || 7.32.60 ||
translation: ततो then, अर्जुनेन by Arjuna, क्रुद्धेन enraged, सर्वप्राणेन with all his might, सा that, गदा mace, स्तनयोरन्तरे between the breasts, मुक्ता thrown, रावणस्य of Ravana, महोरसि on the great chest.
explanation: Then, the enraged Arjuna, with all his might, hurled that mace at Ravana's broad chest, between his breasts.

shloka_text: वरदानकृतत्राणे सा गदा रावणोरसि । दुर्बलेव यथावेगं द्विधाभूत्वा ऽपतत्क्षितौ ।। 7.32.61 ।।
transliteration: varadānakṛtatrāṇe sā gadā rāvaṇorasi | durbaleva yathāvegaṃ dvidhābhūtvā 'patatkṣitau || 7.32.61 ||
translation: वरदानकृतत्राणे protected by boons, सा that, गदा mace, रावणोरसि on Ravana's chest, दुर्बलेव as if weak, यथावेगं with its full force, द्विधाभूत्वा splitting into two, अपतत्क्षितौ fell on the ground.
explanation: That mace, striking Ravana's chest which was protected by boons, split into two and fell to the ground as if it were weak, despite its full force.

shloka_text: स त्वर्जुनप्रमुक्तेन गदापातेन रावणः । अपासर्पद्धनुर्मात्रं निषसाद च निष्टनन् ।। 7.32.62 ।।
transliteration: sa tvarjunapramuktena gadāpātena rāvaṇaḥ | apāsarpaddhanurmātraṃ niṣasāda ca niṣṭanan || 7.32.62 ||
translation: स he, तु but, अर्जुनप्रमुक्तेन by Arjuna released, गदापातेन by the impact of the mace, रावणः Ravana, अपासर्पत् recoiled, धनुर्मात्रं a bow's length, निषसाद sat down, च and, निष्टनन् groaning.
explanation: But Ravana, struck by the mace released by Arjuna, recoiled a bow's length, sat down, and groaned.

shloka_text: स विह्वलं तदालक्ष्य दशग्रीवं ततो ऽर्जुनः । सहसोत्पत्य जग्राह गरुत्मानिव पन्नगम् ।। 7.32.63 ।।
transliteration: sa vihvalaṃ tadālakṣya daśagrīvaṃ tato 'rjunaḥ | sahasotpatya jagrāha garutmāniva pannagam || 7.32.63 ||
translation: स he, विह्वलं bewildered, तत् that, आलक्ष्य having seen, दशग्रीवं Dashagriva, ततो then, अर्जुनः Arjuna, सहसा suddenly, उत्पत्य leaping up, जग्राह seized, गरुत्मानिव like Garuda, पन्नगम् a serpent.
explanation: Perceiving Dashagriva to be bewildered, Arjuna then suddenly leaped up and seized him, just as Garuda seizes a serpent.

shloka_text: स तु बाहुसहस्रेण बलाद्गृह्य दशाननम् । बबन्ध बलवान्राजा बलिं नारायणो यथा ।। 7.32.64 ।।
transliteration: sa tu bāhusahasreṇa balādgṛhya daśānanam | babandha balavānrājā baliṃ nārāyaṇo yathā || 7.32.64 ||
translation: सः He, तु indeed, बाहुसहस्रेण with a thousand arms, बलात् by force, गृह्य having seized, दशाननम् Daśānana (Rāvaṇa), बबन्ध bound, बलवान् powerful, राजा king, बलिम् Bali, नारायणः Nārāyaṇa, यथा just as.
explanation: The powerful King Kārtavīrya Arjuna, using his thousand arms, forcibly seized Daśānana (Rāvaṇa) and bound him, just as Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) had bound Bali.

shloka_text: बध्यमाने दशग्रीवे सिद्धचारणदेवताः । साध्वीतिवादिनः पुष्पैः किरन्त्यर्जुनमूर्धनि ।। 7.32.65 ।।
transliteration: badhyamāne daśagrīve siddhacāraṇadevatāḥ | sādhvītivādinaḥ puṣpaiḥ kirantyarjunamūrdhani || 7.32.65 ||
translation: बध्यमाने while being bound, दशग्रीवे Daśagrīva, सिद्धचारणदेवताः Siddhas, Chāraṇas, and deities, साध्वीतिवादिनः saying "excellent!", पुष्पैः with flowers, किरन्ति scattered, अर्जुनमूर्धनि on Arjuna's head.
explanation: As Daśagrīva was being bound, the Siddhas, Chāraṇas, and deities, exclaiming "excellent!", scattered flowers upon Arjuna's head.

shloka_text: व्याघ्रो मृगमिवादाय मृगराडिव दन्तिनम् । ननाद हैहयो राजा हर्षादम्बुदवन्मुहुः ।। 7.32.66 ।।
transliteration: vyāghro mṛgamivādāya mṛgarāḍiva dantinam | nanāda haihayo rājā harṣādambudavanmuhuḥ || 7.32.66 ||
translation: व्याघ्रः a tiger, मृगम् a deer, इव like, आदाय having seized, मृगराट् a lion, इव like, दन्तिनम् an elephant, ननाद roared, हैहयः Haihaya, राजा king, हर्षात् from joy, अम्बुदवत् like a cloud, मुहुः repeatedly.
explanation: The Haihaya king (Kārtavīrya Arjuna) roared repeatedly with joy, like a tiger seizing a deer or a lion capturing an elephant, and like a thundering cloud.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तस्तु समाश्वस्तो दृष्ट्वा बद्धं दशाननम् । सह तै राक्षसैः क्रुद्धश्चाभिदुद्राव पार्थिवम् ।। 7.32.67 ।।
transliteration: prahastastu samāśvasto dṛṣṭvā baddhaṃ daśānanam | saha tai rākṣasaiḥ kruddhaścābhidudrāva pārthivam || 7.32.67 ||
translation: प्रहस्तः Prahasta, तु but, समाश्वस्तः having recovered, दृष्ट्वा having seen, बद्धम् bound, दशाननम् Daśānana, सह with, तैः those, राक्षसैः Rākṣasas, क्रुद्धः enraged, च and, अभिदुद्राव rushed towards, पार्थिवम् the king.
explanation: But Prahasta, having recovered from his shock upon seeing Daśānana bound, became enraged and, along with those Rākṣasas, rushed towards the king.

shloka_text: नक्तञ्चराणां वेगस्तु तेषामापततां बभौ । उद्भूत आतपापाये पयोदानामिवाम्बुधौ ।। 7.32.68 ।।
transliteration: naktañcarāṇāṃ vegastu teṣāmāpatatāṃ babhau | udbhūta ātapāpāye payodānāmivāmbudhau || 7.32.68 ||
translation: नक्तञ्चराणाम् of the night-wanderers, वेगः the rush, तु indeed, तेषाम् of them, आपतताम् who were rushing, बभौ appeared, उद्भूतः arisen, आतपापाये at the end of the hot season, पयोदानाम् of clouds, इव like, अम्बुधौ in the ocean.
explanation: The rush of those charging Rākṣasas appeared like the gathering of monsoon clouds over the ocean at the end of the hot season.

shloka_text: मुञ्च मुञ्चेति भाषन्तस्तिष्ठतिष्ठेति चासकृत् । मुसलानि सशूलानि सोत्ससर्ज तदार्जुने ।। 7.32.69 ।।
transliteration: muñca muñceti bhāṣantastiṣṭhatiṣṭheti cāsakṛt | musalāni saśūlāni sotsasarja tadārjune || 7.32.69 ||
translation: मुञ्च मुञ्चेति "release, release" thus, भाषन्तः speaking, तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति "stop, stop" thus, च and, असकृत् repeatedly, मुसलानि maces, सशूलानि with spears, सः he (Ravana's army), उत्ससर्ज hurled, तदा then, अर्जुने at Arjuna.
explanation: Then, Ravana's army repeatedly hurled maces and spears at Arjuna, shouting "release, release" and "stop, stop."

shloka_text: अप्राप्तान्येव तान्याशु असम्भ्रान्तस्तदार्जुनः । आयुधान्यमरारीणां जग्राहारिनिषूदनः ।। 7.32.70 ।।
transliteration: aprāptānyeva tānyāśu asambhrāntastadārjunaḥ | āyudhānyamarārīṇāṃ jagrāhāriniṣūdanaḥ || 7.32.70 ||
translation: अप्राप्तानि not yet reached, एव just, तानि those (weapons), आशु quickly, असम्भ्रान्तः undisturbed, तदा then, अर्जुनः Arjuna, आयुधानि weapons, अमरारीणाम् of the enemies of gods, जग्राह caught, अरिनिषूदनः the destroyer of enemies.
explanation: Then, the undisturbed Arjuna, the destroyer of enemies, quickly caught those weapons of the Rakshasas even before they reached him.

shloka_text: ततस्तैरेव रक्षांसि दुर्धरैः प्रवरायुधैः । भित्त्वा विद्रावयामास वायुरम्बुधरानिव ।। 7.32.71 ।।
transliteration: tatastaireva rakṣāṃsi durdharaiḥ pravarāyudhaiḥ | bhittvā vidrāvayāmāsa vāyurambudharāniva || 7.32.71 ||
translation: ततः then, तैः by those, एव just, रक्षांसि the Rakshasas, दुर्धरैः formidable, प्रवरायुधैः with excellent weapons, भित्त्वा having pierced, विद्रावयामास made to flee, वायुः wind, अम्बुधरान् clouds, इव like.
explanation: Then, with those very formidable and excellent weapons, Arjuna pierced and dispersed the Rakshasas, just as the wind scatters clouds.

shloka_text: राक्षसांस्त्रासयित्वा तु कार्तवीर्यो ऽर्जुनस्तदा । रावणं गृह्य नगरं प्रविवेश सुहृद्वृतः ।। 7.32.72 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasāṃstrāsayitvā tu kārtavīryo 'rjunastadā | rāvaṇaṃ gṛhya nagaraṃ praviveśa suhṛdvṛtaḥ || 7.32.72 ||
translation: राक्षसान् the Rakshasas, त्रासयित्वा having frightened, तु and, कार्तवीर्यः Kartavirya, अर्जुनः Arjuna, तदा then, रावणम् Ravana, गृह्य having seized, नगरम् the city, प्रविवेश entered, सुहृद्वृतः surrounded by friends.
explanation: Then, after frightening the Rakshasas, Kartavirya Arjuna seized Ravana and entered the city, surrounded by his friends.

shloka_text: स कीर्यमाणः कुसुमाक्षतोत्करैर्द्विजैः सपौरैः पुरुहूतसन्निभः । तदा ऽर्जुनः सम्प्रविवेश तां पुरीं बलिं निगृह्येव सहस्रलोचनः ।। 7.32.73 ।।
transliteration: sa kīryamāṇaḥ kusumākṣatotkarairdvijaiḥ sapauraiḥ puruhūtasannibhaḥ | tadā 'rjunaḥ sampraviveśa tāṃ purīṃ baliṃ nigṛhyeva sahasralocanaḥ || 7.32.73 ||
translation: सः he (Arjuna), कीर्यमाणः being showered, कुसुमाक्षतोत्करैः with heaps of flowers and unbroken rice grains, द्विजैः by Brahmins, सपौरैः along with citizens, पुरुहूतसन्निभः resembling Puruhuta (Indra), तदा then, अर्जुनः Arjuna, सम्प्रविवेश entered, ताम् that, पुरीम् city, बलिम् Bali, निगृह्य having captured, इव like, सहस्रलोचनः the thousand-eyed one (Indra).
explanation: Then, Arjuna, resembling Indra, entered that city, being showered with heaps of flowers and unbroken rice grains by Brahmins and citizens, just as the thousand-eyed Indra entered after capturing Bali. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 32 ।। Thus ends the thirty-second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
